justification: Removes five invented real-world values from the setbacks path and replaces four separate area implementations with one scale-corrected function in lib/geometry/mercator.ts, which IS live (imported by lot-dimensions.ts and lot-shape-analysis.ts). Not Critical: measured, the entire setbacks-calculate feature is unreachable -- no route mounts AnalysisTabs, PreciseSetbackCalculator or EnhancedSetbackVerification, lib/geometry/calculator.ts has no consumer, and the endpoint's only other caller sends `zone` where the schema requires `property_zone` and therefore always 400s. No user saw these figures. Not Minor: it changes a live module's public surface (two new exports), narrows BuildableAreaAnalysis from number to number|null across the response contract, and removes code that would have shipped wrong numbers the moment anyone mounted the feature.

pre_impl.existing_data: lib/geometry/mercator.ts already existed as the stated single source of truth for EPSG:3857 rings, its correction calibrated against surveyed area on title over 577,081 single-part cadastre lots, and its own header already said to import from it rather than carry a local latitude constant. The fix adds ringAreaM2 and lotGeometryAreaM2 there instead of writing a fourth implementation, and lib/geometry/calculator.ts now delegates to it.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Two of my own claims this session were wrong and were corrected by measurement rather than by argument. First, I said the invented lot area fires on the automatic path and was not latent; I had read the call-site code without checking whether the call site is mounted, and nothing mounts it, so all five values are latent. Second, the nearby estimator looked like a 45 percent overstatement, but reproducing its arithmetic showed it returns exactly 100 for every lot below 99,217 square metres, which is a constant for every residential lot in NSW rather than an approximation.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Four area implementations reduced to one. Deleted the uncorrected shoelace in EnhancedSetbackVerification, the bounding-box estimator in PreciseSetbackCalculator, and the duplicated loop in calculator.ts, which is now a delegation. Deliberately left alone: lib/setbacks/validator.ts estimateLotArea, a hardcoded zone-to-lot-area table with R2 at 500 and a fallback of 450. It is pre-existing dead code whose only reference is a doc comment inside its own index.ts, and the standing rule is not to touch pre-existing dead code, so it is flagged rather than fixed.
pre_impl.external_source_error: No external source is called anywhere in this change. The Mercator correction is arithmetic on the ring's own northing, so there is no network failure mode to handle.
pre_impl.frontend_type: BuildableAreaAnalysis numeric fields narrow from number to number or null, plus an optional unavailable_reason, and both render sites now print Not available for a null following the existing convention in GrannyFlatBriefCard. SetbackCalculationRequest lot_geometry and lot_area become optional to match the endpoint's zod schema, which has had them optional all along; the interface declaring them required is precisely why callers invented values to satisfy the compiler. npx tsc --noEmit exits 0.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Had anyone mounted this feature, the setbacks tab would have shown Total Lot Area 100 square metres, Buildable Area 60 square metres and Buildable Percentage 60 for every property in NSW, with a 9.5 metre height limit and a 0.6 to 1 FSR shown whenever the real controls were absent, and R2 substituted for an unknown zone, which also selects which setback rules the endpoint returns. After this change each of those reads Not available with the reason stated.

falsifiable_check.observed_red: 56 of 56 tests pass on clean code; npx tsc --noEmit exits 0; the full frontend suite is 117 suites and 1666 tests with 0 failures. The real evidence is the mutation harness: 15 mutations applied one at a time and reverted byte-for-byte, 15 of 15 CAUGHT, 0 holes. It found a genuine hole on its first run -- expect(src).toMatch(/lotGeometryAreaM2/) was satisfied by the IMPORT line, so replacing the real call with = 450 left the suite green. Fixed by requiring a call site's trailing paren and asserting lot_area is never assigned a numeric literal; that mutation is now caught.

functions.name: ringAreaM2
functions.input: An unknown value expected to be an EPSG:3857 ring, validated through usableRing so every point must be a finite two-number pair before any arithmetic runs.
functions.output: The ground area in square metres, divided by the square of the ring's own Mercator scale factor, or null when the ring cannot be measured at all.
functions.if_none: Returns null rather than 0, because 0 is a legitimate area for a degenerate polygon and reads downstream as a measurement; the callers then omit the field instead of substituting a number.

functions.name: lotGeometryAreaM2
functions.input: An unknown value expected to be a Portal lot geometry carrying a rings array, with the ring count checked before the outer ring is read.
functions.output: The outer ring's ground area in square metres for a single-ring geometry, delegating the arithmetic entirely to ringAreaM2 so there is one implementation.
functions.if_none: Returns null for any ring count other than exactly one, because an inner ring is a hole and no caller here subtracts holes, so an outer-ring area would overstate the lot.

functions.name: buildableAreaNotDerived
functions.input: A caller-measured lot area in square metres, or null when the caller did not measure one, and nothing else at all.
functions.output: The single BuildableAreaAnalysis object used by every one of the five response branches, passing the lot area through untouched and leaving every boundary-dependent figure null.
functions.if_none: Sets unavailable_reason to say buildable area needs the lot boundary and that this request resolved setback rules for the zone only, so the absence is stated rather than filled.

values: N/A -- no value is read from a database or an API in this change; every figure removed was a literal in source, and the one figure now computed comes from the request's own geometry.
queries: N/A -- no database query is added or modified. The reachability finding came from grep over app/, components/ and hooks/, not from SQL.

break_it.what_happens: Each of the nine shapes returns null, and the suite additionally asserts the result is never 450, 100, 500, 400 or 0, which are the four old substitutes plus the old return 0 that read as a measured lot size.
break_it.how: usableRing rejects the ring before any arithmetic, and ringAreaM2 returns null rather than a fallback; nine parameterised cases plus five never-equals assertions cover it.

break_it.how: The ring count is tested for exactly one before the outer ring is read, and a mutation relaxing that comparison fails the suite.

break_it.how: Behavioural assertions against known-area rings, plus an assertion that the ratio of the uncorrected to the corrected figure equals the square of the scale factor.

verdicts.finding: MEDIUM type-boundary, lib/geometry/mercator.ts:140 -- lotGeometryAreaM2 can return 0 for a structurally valid but degenerate ring, while the endpoint's schema requires lot_area to be positive and both components submit every non-null result.
verdicts.verdict: CONFIRMED and FIXED. Measured before acting: ringAreaM2([[0,0],[10,0],[20,0],[0,0]]) returned 0, as did an all-same-point ring and a there-and-back ring. The consequence is worse than a misleading figure -- lot_area is z.number().positive(), so a 0 fails validation and returns 400 for the WHOLE request, discarding the zone setback rules that need no area. It also contradicted my own doc comment, which already claimed 'Returns null, never 0'. ringAreaM2 now requires area > 0; three degenerate shapes are asserted null, and the mutation that removes the guard is caught.

verdicts.finding: MEDIUM silent-failure, lib/geometry/calculator.ts:530 -- the new delegation still coalesces an unmeasurable ring to 0 via `?? 0`, silently converting missing or malformed geometry into a plausible numeric area.
verdicts.verdict: CONFIRMED and FIXED. I had kept `?? 0` deliberately to avoid a behaviour change, but having already widened BuildableAreaAnalysis to number|null in this same change, propagating null was type-safe and strictly more honest. estimateLotAreaFromGeometry is renamed lotAreaFromGeometry and returns number|null; all three return paths of calculateBuildableArea now take total_lot_area from one guarded local, and buildable_area / buildable_percentage / setback_area_lost are null rather than 0 on the two paths whose own note says the figure could not be calculated. Three mutations cover it.
